chunks: Al-Kafi: Humayd ibn Ziyad from Ibn Sama'a from Ibn Ribat from Iys ibn al-Qasim from Abi Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about a man who gave his wife the option to choose (Takhyir), and she chose herself, so she was divorced from him? He said: No, this was a matter specific to the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he was ordered to do so and he did it. And if they had chosen themselves, he would have divorced them. And it is the word of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic: 'Say to your wives: if you desire the worldly life and its adornment, then come, I will provide for you and set you free with a goodly release.'
Al-Hasan ibn Sama'a said: By this Hadith we derive the ruling in the matter of Khiyar (option/ultimatum).

key_terms.اختارت نفسها: She chose herself (implying the option to stay or be divorced).
key_terms.الخياري: The legal ruling or principle derived from the narration regarding the option.
key_terms.تخيير: The act of giving someone the option or choice between two things.

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Prophet's right of Takhyir and a husband's general right to grant his wife an option to choose?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that the right of 'Takhyir' (choice) granted to the Prophet’s wives was a specific divine prerogative (khassiyyah) rather than a general legal precedent for all husbands. This distinction is rooted in Surah Al-Ahzab (33:28), where the command to offer divorce if they chose worldly life was a unique directive for the Prophet. Consequently, Shia jurists derive from this that while the principle of choice exists, the specific mechanism of the Prophet's divorce upon their choice does not automatically apply to ordinary men.

en.ammaar-muslim: 13. [13/-] al-Kafi: Humayd b. Ziyad from Ibn Sama’a from Ibn Ribat from Iys b. al-Qasim from Abi Abdillah عليه السلام, he (Iys) said:

I asked him about a man who derogates to his wife the option to choose – so she chooses herself, will this mean that the divorce is final? he said: No, this (i.e. Takhyir) is a thing which was only for the messenger of Allah specifically, he was ordered to do that so he did it, and if they had chosen themselves then he would have divorced them – and it is the words of Allah Mighty and Majestic “Say to your wives: if you prefer the life of this world and its adornment then come forth so that I provide you a provision and set you free in a goodly manner” [33:28].
al-Hasan b. Sama’a said: by this Hadith do we take [rule] in the matter of Khiyar [giving an ultimatum to the wife to decide her future].
